entries.title: Book club notice links to the Book Club pad
entries.summary: The notice that the book club starts on Monday 30 November now has a button to the Book Club pad. The same notice is at the top of the 30 November session page until that meeting is over, and further down the page afterwards.

entries.title: Quorum option on the 23 November ballot: 75% of the active voting body
entries.summary: The host changed the last option of question 1 on the 23 November ballot during council screening, before voting opened: it was 25% of the active voting body and is now 75% of the active voting body. The active voting body is about 28 people (the 24 who voted on the 16 November ballot and 4 more who spoke in the 23 November session), so 25% would be 7 votes, too few to stand for the group; 75% is 21 votes. A dated line under the question says what changed and why. The other options are unchanged.

entries.title: Book club pad: sign up by email
entries.summary: The book club pad now has an email sign-up in its Join section, and a short popup offers the same sign-up when you are about to leave the page.

entries.title: The 23 November ballot opens on its own when council screening closes
entries.summary: The 23 November session page now holds the ballot. Voting opens by itself on Thursday 26 November at 8:00 PM Pacific, when the interim council's screening closes, and runs 72 hours, to Sunday 29 November at 8:00 PM Pacific. Every draft question with no standing objection at the close goes to the ballot as drafted. A question the council held back is shown with the objections and reasons, and cannot be voted on. Anyone signed in can vote, one vote per account, as on 16 November. Yes/No questions use the two-tier rule chosen on 16 November: 60% or more Yes passes, 50% to under 60% stays open for review. The two multiple-choice questions take the option with the most votes. The phase label, banner and call to action follow the clock. Results are published on the page after the close. No question or option changed.

entries.title: Council screening: clearer page, and a clear message when you cannot object
entries.summary: On the 23 November session page, the banner over the draft ballot and the phase label now follow the clock. While the interim council screens, they say that the community review has closed and that the council is screening until Thursday 26 November, 8:00 PM Pacific, before the 72-hour community vote. When the window closes they say so without another update. A signed-in visitor who is not on the interim council is now told who they are signed in as and that only council members can object. If the council list cannot be loaded, the page says so instead of hiding the button without a word. No ballot question or option changed.

entries.title: Corrected quorum note on the 23 November ballot
entries.summary: The note under question 1 of the 23 November draft ballot said the active voting body was the 76 people the session emails go to. The host corrected it on 25 November, after the review closed: those 76 people are the voting body (25% is 19 votes), and the active voting body is the people who have voted in a ballot or taken part in a session during the pilot, 28 people as of 25 November (25% is 7 votes). A dated line under the note says what changed. The question and its options are unchanged.

entries.title: Pad votes: the site's server signs in to Gov Hub with the right key
entries.summary: When the site reads pad votes from Gov Hub as its own server (council seats, support and objection lists, moving the existing votes), it now uses the key production Gov Hub expects. Nothing changes for visitors.

entries.title: Staging keeps pad votes on Gov Hub
entries.summary: On the staging site, session ballots, pad support and concern, supports, screening objections and the voter list now read and write Gov Hub. The existing staging votes were moved there first, and the counts and voter list matched. Production is unchanged until its own move.

entries.title: Pad votes can be kept on Gov Hub
entries.summary: Session ballots, proposal pad support and concern, next-session supports and council screening objections can now be stored on Gov Hub instead of this site, behind a switch that stays off until the existing votes are moved. Gov Hub keeps who voted apart from how they voted. If Gov Hub can't be reached, voting pauses with a clear message, and an outage of more than an hour moves the close later. The public voter list no longer shows non-abstain counts, which hinted at how someone voted; streaks now count the ballots someone voted on. Council screening uses the council's seats on Gov Hub.

entries.title: Linked accounts sign in as one person
entries.summary: When someone has linked two Gov Hub accounts, signing in with either one now opens the site as their main account. A session opened before the link is moved to the main account, so steering seats, co-editor seats and votes belong to one person.

entries.title: Overweb Book Club pad
entries.summary: A new pad, /pads/book-club, holds every book club meeting: pick the chapter at the top. Before a meeting the featured reading, prompts and extra credit are on top, with a way to join and to propose something for the meeting. During the meeting the chat moves to the top for questions and insights. After it, the meeting summary, the review draft, proposals and votes come first and the reading moves down. Each meeting has its own chat, an Ask Deepi about the reading, and Invite others.

entries.title: Propose something for the next session
entries.summary: Every session page now has a box to put a proposal on the next session's agenda. Sign in, give your real name, a one-line proposal and a few sentences on why. It shows at once on the next session's page under "Proposals for this session", labelled "Participant proposal", and on the Ballot options pad. Others can support it with one click; the proposer can withdraw it; an interim council member can hide spam or an off-topic proposal, with a public reason. Proposals close when the session starts.

entries.title: Who proposed each ballot option, and who has been voting
entries.summary: Every option on the 16 November ballot and the 23 November draft ballot now shows, in small text under it, who proposed it, who seconded or supported it, and whether it was approved, with links to the moment in the transcript. A new page, Ballot options (under Pads and in the Events menu), lists every option, decisions taken in the meeting and the 30 November proposals, filterable by status and searchable by name. It also lists who has voted: ballots voted, non-abstain votes and weekly streak, never how anyone voted. Anyone can hide their name from that list on their account page.

entries.title: Book club: bring a question or insight
entries.summary: The book club invitation on the 23 November page and the 30 November session description now ask people to bring a question or insight, instead of a passage.

entries.title: 30 November agenda: Version 1.1 by December, Nautilus entry, and book revenue
entries.summary: Session pages can now list proposals put forward for the session. The 30 November session lists two: publish Version 1.1 by 31 December, put it on sale and enter it for the 2027 Nautilus Book Awards (categories 31 and 26) by 8 February; and, separately, where any revenue from the book should go.

entries.title: Each listening session has its own review doc, made ahead of time
entries.summary: The 30 November, 7 December and 14 December sessions now each have their own review Google Doc, created ahead of time and recorded with the session, so every session page links its own doc for comments.

entries.title: 23 November session has its own review Google Doc
entries.summary: The 23 November draft is now in its own Google Doc, open for comments by anyone with the link, and the session page's review box links to it, with the session chat and email as alternatives. Each session has its own review doc; none links an earlier session's.

entries.title: Review boxes default to the session's own chat

entries.title: Council screening works by no objection

A question goes to the ballot unless a council member objects in writing with a reason; anything held back is published with that reason. If the council does not act in time, the question goes forward as drafted.

entries.title: Session pages follow the voted rules: 48-hour review, 72-hour vote

entries.title: Today's session page shows last week's ballot results
entries.summary: The 23 November session page now reads out the results of the 16 November ballot: the outcome of each question, the 24 voters, and the quorum tie, with a link to the full counts on the 16 November page. Its text now says voting has closed.

entries.title: Votes and DP sign-ins record how the person arrived: the message tag and any Canopi referral
entries.summary: Any page opened with a message tag (?ref=em-1122-closes, wa-1122-lastcall, inv-email and so on) or a Canopi referral (ref_token or canopi_ref_token, a referrer's Canopi user id as canopi_ref or ?ref=<uuid>, ch, utm_source/medium/campaign, or an embed referralCode) now sets a first-party cookie, dp_arrival (30 days, SameSite=Lax, HttpOnly), holding the first and latest tag and the first referral. In ?ref= a slug is a message tag and a UUID is a referrer, never mixed. It holds nothing about the visitor; tags name a message, never a person. It is set on the server before the page renders, so pages that take ?ref off the address bar do not lose it. When an account first submits a ballot, the tags, a short referral label (never the token), channel and campaign are stored once in dp_ballot_vote_attribution; later edits do not change it, and it plays no part in counting. Sign-in from the DP site passes the DP embed instance and the referral to Canopi's sign-up (canopiId, referralCode, refToken verbatim, and ref when it is a UUID; Canopi records a referrer for new accounts only, a valid token winning over ref) and keeps the account's first arrival in dp_account_attribution. ballot-admin attribution prints counts per tag and per referral, never accounts. Requested by the owner on 22 Nov 2026.

entries.title: Pads: an Invite others panel on every proposal pad and session page
entries.summary: Every proposal pad and community session page now has an Invite others panel. It offers Copy link, the phone's share sheet, a QR code (made on the page, no outside service), an Email link with a prefilled subject and body, share links for WhatsApp, Telegram, LinkedIn, X and Bluesky, and a Copy message for Signal button. The text comes from the pad: its title, plain-language summary and current call to action (add your view, vote, join on Monday). Links carry ?ref=inv-<channel>, which names the channel and never a person, so arrivals can be counted per channel. Signed-in accounts can also send from the site: up to 5 addresses per send and 20 per account per day, with the sender's name and an optional short note with no links. An address is invited to the same pad at most once every 30 days and gets at most 3 invitations a day, and the site sends at most 300 a day. Opted-out addresses are skipped. Only a keyed hash of each address is stored, for these limits, and rows are deleted after 35 days. Nobody is added to a list. Every email says why it came and has an opt-out link. Requested by the owner on 21 Nov 2026.

entries.title: Proposal pads: one page per proposal, explained in plain terms, with the record and a way to weigh in
entries.summary: Every DP proposal now has a pad at /pads/proposals/<id> (the 8-character id or the full id). The pad shows the DP and a short title, the status with the "Reopened for Version 1.1" marker, and how many co-editor approvals it has of the number needed. A plain-language summary (AI-generated by Claude Opus 5.5 ahead of time and stored, labelled as such; the proposal text is authoritative) explains it for newcomers. The change is shown before and after inside the current chapter text with the anchor highlighted, and a proposal whose passage is gone says "Passage no longer in the chapter: needs re-anchoring". The record lists the proposer, filed date, rationale, a history built from approvals, steering votes and outcomes, the reopen and the revised-from chain, the decision notes, the steering analysis from the closed (public) steering stages, related proposals and the DPs it touches. Co-editors of that DP get Approve, Revise and Decline through the existing Review flow. Anyone signed in can give an advisory Support or Concern with an optional one-line reason (one per account, changeable; counts and reasons are public, names only if the voter chooses), under a rule setting (PAD_DECISION_RULE, default co-editors decide). Deepi (the site chat) opens scoped to the proposal, using the page context the session pages added. Signed-in people can follow a pad; a sweep emails followers when its status changes, with the token unsubscribe link, but stays off until PAD_FOLLOW_EMAILS=on. /pads lists the proposal pads for open items, with room for other pad types; /improve/open-items and the Review tab link to each pad.

entries.title: Attach images to an Acknowledgements change request
entries.summary: The form at /acknowledgements/request has an optional "Attach an image" field: up to three images (a screenshot of the problem, a photo, or proof of a contribution), JPEG, PNG or WebP, 5 MB each, with previews and Remove buttons. On phones the picker offers the camera and the photo library; iPhones hand HEIC photos over as JPEG, and an HEIC file that still arrives is refused with a message saying how to send it as JPEG. Signing in stays optional. The site's server checks each file by its first bytes and uploads it to Gov Hub, which re-encodes it from its pixels (no EXIF, GPS, XMP or comments survive), stores it privately with the request and shows it only to the steering committee and super admins on the Gov Hub review page. Images never appear on public pages or in any other API response. Uploads are rate-limited on Gov Hub; a rejected image stops the request before anything is sent.
